reasons: Correctly identifies a genuine deviation: p0042's 'Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested' is a mandatory, uncapped, term-long sole-source purchase (tie-in) obligation on Customer, which the rule's detection guidance covers ('shall purchase all of its requirements from').

Redline reaches the preferred position by converting the obligation to optional ('Client may, at its option, order from TrueLink') and confirming no exclusive/sole-source purchasing obligation; it leaves TrueLink's transmission duty and the non-exclusive licence grant (which benefits Client) untouched, consistent with 'keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer'.

Edit is directionally correct and reasonably minimal — the changed-character ratio (0.54) reflects the necessary rewrite of one sentence plus a short protective proviso; the incidental fix of 'order TrueLink' to 'order from TrueLink' does not alter substance.

Comment is accurate, in-house voice, cites the playbook position, and offers the correct fallback (credit-report category, 12 months, automatic termination on failure of the Section 3/4 response-time, availability and support commitments).

Severity moderated to medium: the commitment is confined to a single product category (credit reports) and only bites when Client voluntarily uses the Interface, since Section 2(a) expressly states Client is not obligated to use the licence and may develop or licence competing systems — nearer the fallback than the walk-away position, though the missing term limit and performance exit still warrant the edit.
